html:
Mohammed V was the sultan and then king of Morocco who led it to independence from France in 1956. He reigned from 1927 until his death in 1961.

At first a figurehead under the French protectorate, he came to back the nationalist Istiqlal party, which demanded independence in 1944. In 1953 the French deposed him and exiled him to Corsica and Madagascar. The exile made him a national hero, and unrest spread.

France brought him back in November 1955, and Morocco became independent on 2 March 1956; Spain gave up its northern zone soon after. In 1957 he took the title of king. His son Hassan II succeeded him. See also French Morocco.
